findings.title: Three mdrep questions are word-for-word repeats of first-test questions. v9's only miss on mdrep, and all of rule 4's +0.021, come from one of them
findings.evidence: These mdrep questions have the same normalised text as first-test questions: issue_pr_author-author-031 = mdplan issue_pr_author-author-037; ticket_link-status-038 = mdplan ticket_link-status-039; person_first-006 = mdplan person_first-008; and person_count-005 = mdplan_w1 person_count-007. They come from the same wording template with the same key or person (ENG-4823, Jordan Lee). Every pair has a different expected answer and no gold document in common, so these are different entities that reuse a key or name. The only v9 miss on mdrep is ticket_link-status-038, 'Ticket ENG-4823 is linked to another ticket. Could you please tell me where that other ticket currently stands?' (v9 answered 'Marco Diaz' via dependencies→assignee; expected 'In Progress'). v9 also missed the identical text in the first test (answered 'ENG-4822'; expected 'In Review'). v10's form for this text was the same in both runs; v10 was wrong on mdplan and right on mdrep. If the 3 identical-text questions are dropped, mdrep scores v4 0.587, v8 0.738, v9 1.000, v9n 0.976, v10 1.000.
findings.impact: There is no leakage, and rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 and the 0.925 level do not change. But the new set's single v9 error repeats a wording failure already seen in the first test; it is not a new, independent observation. The rule-4 difference of +0.021 rests on that one question (v10 − v9 = 0 without it). It should not be read as a sign that v10's form helps on the new documents.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every number in the finding matches the data. The repository was not changed; my two scripts are in scratchpad/refute_dup.

What I checked:
- **Repeated text.** I compared normalised question text in mdrep and its wording folders against mdplan and its wording folders, and against the earlier sets (mdtrain, mdtrainv9, mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm).
  - Matches with the first test on the drawn wording: issue_pr_author-author-031 = mdplan issue_pr_author-author-037, ticket_link-status-038 = mdplan ticket_link-status-039, and person_first-006 = mdplan person_first-008.
  - Also, mdrep person_count-005 = mdplan_w1 person_count-007.
  - No mdrep question matches any older set.
  - Each pair has a different expected answer (Anika Patel / Dylan Brooks, In Progress / In Review, DES-7319 / PM-914007, 4 / 3) and no gold document in common. The two ENG-4823 tickets are different documents with different titles, one about dashboard links and one about a workload generator.
- **Misses.** Recomputed with mdrep/plan_report.json, which is identical to the committed replication/plan_report.json.
  - v9's only miss on mdrep is ticket_link-status-038: it answered 'Marco Diaz' via dependencies → assignee; the expected answer is 'In Progress'.
  - On mdplan ticket_link-status-039, v9 answered 'ENG-4822' and v10 answered 'Done'; the expected answer is 'In Review'.
  - v10's form was the same in both runs: kind 'other', fields [status, state], raw answer 'status'.
- **Scores.** Means are of the link, combine and compare group means. Dropping the 3 repeated questions gives v4 0.587, v8 0.738, v9 1.000, v9n 0.976, v10 1.000. Without ticket_link-status-038, v9's link score is 15/15, so v10 − v9 = 0.

Two further checks support the finding:
- The miss comes from the wording. On mdrep, v9 gets this question right ('In Progress') in writer 2's and writer 3's wordings. It fails only in writer 1's 'where that other ticket currently stands', which was the drawn wording in both tests. On mdrep_w1, v9 also misses ticket_link-status-027 in the same wording.
- docs/FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md (lines 86–92 and 131–133) already names this wording as v9's weak point.

Two qualifications:
1. The repeats follow from the pre-registered design: the same wordings are reused, documents rather than question texts are excluded, and the benchmark reuses keys and names across documents. So this is not a protocol breach, and rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 and the 0.925 level stand.
2. 'Different entities' overstates the Jordan Lee case. It may be the same person's name; what differs is the set of documents. The write-up should say 'different documents'.

The +0.021 is already inside the pre-registration's noise band (0.04 or less), so this changes how the write-up reads the result, not any published number or verdict.

findings.title: Reused ticket key: one question has the same kind and expected answer as a first-test question and a training question, but it is a different ticket. Effect: none
findings.evidence: compare_two-049 asks 'ENG-51399 vs ENG-4823, which one's due first?' (expected ENG-4823). It has the same kind and the same expected key as mdplan compare_two-045 (DES-14201 vs ENG-4823) and as training mdtrain compare_two-043 / mdtrainv9 compare_two-184, 185 and 186 (ENG-13750 vs ENG-4823). No gold document is shared. ENG-4823's due date is 2026-02-14 here, 2026-02-07 in the first test and 2025-02-24 in training, and the other ticket differs each time. No key, value, date or person from mdrep's questions appears literally in plan_lessons_v4, v8, v9 or v9n.json, and each bank holds only its own 50 documents. Inside mdrep, ENG-4823 belongs to a single document (dsid_cd9a74e5…), which underlies 4 of the 50 questions (author-031, status-038, due_date-030, compare-049). No other key belongs to more than one document in the mdrep bank.
findings.impact: The answer cannot be recalled from training or from the first test. Every arm, v4 included, answers it right. Dropping it leaves v9, v9n and v10 compare at 1.000 and moves v4 and v8 by less than 0.01. The only point to note is clustering: 8% of questions depend on one Linear document, and that includes v9's one miss.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute the finding and could not. Its facts check out in the data, and the effect is as small as it says, so no score or rule verdict changes.

What I checked:
- **The three questions:** mdrep compare_two-049 (ENG-51399 vs ENG-4823), mdplan compare_two-045 (DES-14201 vs ENG-4823), mdtrain compare_two-043 and mdtrainv9/mdtrainall compare_two-184, 185 and 186 (ENG-13750 vs ENG-4823) all expect ENG-4823. No gold document is shared between them.
- **Three different tickets:** the three ENG-4823 source documents are unrelated tickets.
  - mdrep, dsid_cd9a74e5: "Add canonical dashboard links to Support runbooks…", due 2026-02-14, assignee Allison Grant.
  - mdplan, dsid_bf69afe8: "Representative chat streaming workload generator…", due 2026-02-07, assignee Rina Kobayashi.
  - mdtrain, dsid_58405bc2: "Python SDK: refresh streaming…", due 2025-02-24, assignee Sabrina James.
- **Each bank holds its own 50 documents:** the bank's sources are exactly the 50 haystack dsids in mdrep, mdplan and mdtrain.
- **One document per key in mdrep:** there are 34 key facts and 34 key aliases, and no key or alias maps to more than one document. eng-4823 maps only to doc:dsid_cd9a74e5. That document is a gold document for exactly 4 questions: author-031, status-038, due_date-030 and compare_two-049.
- **No lesson or glossary leak:** I took 98 values from mdrep's questions (keys, expected values, pieces, PR numbers, quoted titles). None appears in mdtrain/plan_lessons_v4, v8, v9 or v9n.json, fb50/lessons.json, or either glossary. The only hits were the digits 2, 3 and 4, and "391" inside a float weight in v9. The v10 forms only hold each question's own text.
- **Scores on own answers:** v4, v8, v9, v9n and v10 all answer compare_two-049 correctly; v1 does not (it answered 2026-04-01). Dropping the question leaves v9, v9n and v10 unchanged, with compare at 1.000. v4 and v8 each move −0.006 (0.580→0.574 and 0.720→0.714), and the same holds on the changed copy.
- **v9's one miss:** it is ticket_link-status-038, which rests on dsid_cd9a74e5.

Corrections to the finding:
1. **v1:** "Every arm" means v4–v10; v1 gets it wrong.
2. **Right for the right reason:** v4's correct answer does not count on this measure (reason = 0). On this measure, dropping the question moves v4 by +0.030 (0.471→0.501) and v8 by −0.012 (0.678→0.666). So "less than 0.01" holds only for own answers. Rule 3 is still met: the v9−v4 margin goes from 0.508 to 0.478.
3. **Clustering is not special to this document:** two other documents each underlie 5 of the 50 questions (10%). One is dsid_1fb9a5cc, ENG-51399's document and the other gold document of compare_two-049; the other is dsid_d223007d. Six more documents underlie 4 questions each.
4. **More reuse with the first test than the finding says:** two more mdrep questions have the same wording, kind and keys as first-test questions, with different answers.
   - ticket_link-status-038 matches mdplan ticket_link-status-039 word for word, and the linked ticket is ENG-4821 both times. The answers differ: In Progress now, In Review in the first test.
   - issue_pr_author-author-031 matches mdplan issue_pr_author-author-037 word for word. The answers differ: Anika Patel vs Dylan Brooks.
   - v9 and v9n missed the ticket_link question in both tests (ENG-4822 then, Marco Diaz now). So v9's one replication miss repeats a first-test miss on the same template and key pair, though in different documents.

Effect on the write-up: the numbers and verdicts do not change. A short note is enough.
verdict.corrected: Suggested write-up note: "Ticket key ENG-4823 occurs in the training set, the first test and this replication. Each time it belongs to a different, unrelated Linear ticket: different document, title, due date and assignee. No document is shared between the sets, no key or value from the new questions appears in the lessons or the glossary, and inside each bank every key belongs to one document. One new question, compare_two-049 (ENG-51399 vs ENG-4823), has the same kind and the same expected answer (ENG-4823) as first-test compare_two-045 and training compare_two-043/184–186. v4, v8, v9, v9n and v10 answer it correctly (v1 does not). v4 is not right for the right reason on it. Dropping it leaves v9, v9n and v10 unchanged. On own answers it lowers v4 and v8 by 0.006 each. On right-for-the-right-reason it raises v4 by 0.030 and lowers v8 by 0.012. No rule changes. Two further questions repeat the first test's wording and keys but have different answers: ticket_link-status-038 (ENG-4823 linked to ENG-4821; In Progress vs In Review) and issue_pr_author-author-031 (Anika Patel vs Dylan Brooks). v9 and v9n missed the ticket_link question in both tests, so v9's one miss here repeats a first-test miss on the same template. Questions cluster on documents throughout the set: ENG-4823's document underlies 4 of the 50 questions; two other documents underlie 5 each and six others 4 each."

findings.title: The new set has fewer questions of v9's weakest kind; with the first test's kind mix, drawn v9 is 0.959, not 0.979
findings.evidence: mdrep's link group is issue_pr_author 5, pr_issue 8 and ticket_link 3; the first test had 5, 7 and 7. ticket_link is v9's weakest kind: first test 0.857 (w1 0.429); mdrep 0.667 drawn, 0.333 for w1. Reweighting mdrep's per-kind scores to mdplan's kind counts gives: drawn v9 0.959, v9n 0.944, v10 1.000, v4 0.584, v8 0.711; w1 v9 0.918 (reported 0.958; first test 0.922); w3 v9 0.900 (reported 0.878). The draw used the same `fresh` rule (at most 8 units per kind), so this is not a departure.
findings.impact: The level rule still passes with the first test's mix (0.959 ≥ 0.925). But part of the closeness of drawn 0.979 to 0.975, and of the single-writer w1 gain from 0.922 to 0.958, comes from the new set having only 3 ticket_link questions, not from v9 doing better.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. I re-ran cie.eval.factbank_multi.measure() read-only on all nine folders. It reproduces every reported score. The headline is a mean of three group scores (link, combine, compare), and each group score is the share of its questions answered right (gm() in factbank_multi.py), so the mix of kinds inside the link group does change the headline.

Kind counts:
- mdrep: issue_pr_author 5, pr_issue 8, ticket_link 3; action_owner_issues 9, person_count 9, person_first 8, compare_two 8.
- mdplan: 5, 7, 7; then 8, 8, 7, 8.

The low ticket_link count is a side effect of fresh(), not a departure from it. fresh() fills action, then pr, then ticket, then person units until it reaches 50 documents, at most 8 units per kind. Both runs used it (seed 37 and seed 41).

Scoring mdrep's per-kind rates with mdplan's counts reproduces every figure in the finding:
- drawn wordings: v9 0.959, v9n 0.944, v10 1.000, v4 0.584, v8 0.711
- writer 1: v9 0.918; writer 3: v9 0.900

I also ran the reverse check, scoring the first test's per-kind rates with the new set's mix. That gives drawn v9 0.984 (against 0.979) and writer-1 v9 0.957 (against 0.958). So whichever mix is shared, v9 does not do better on the new set.
- Drawn: −0.005 to −0.016, instead of the reported +0.004.
- Writer 1: −0.004 to +0.001, instead of +0.036.

Both are inside the pre-registered noise band of 0.04.

The cause is narrower than "ticket_link is weak". Every v9 ticket_link miss in either test is a status question in writer 1's wording ("where that other ticket currently stands"):
- Writer-1 runs: 0 of 6 (mdplan 020, 025, 026, 039; mdrep 027, 038).
- The only drawn-set misses (mdplan 039 and mdrep 038, two different documents that share the key ENG-4823) are status questions that drew writer 1's wording.
- Assignee questions and writer 2's status wording pass every time.

The new set had 2 ticket_link status questions; the first had 4. That is why the writer-1 link score rose.

Corrections to the finding:
1. For writer 1, all of the gain from 0.922 to 0.958 comes from the mix, not just "part of" it.
2. Writer 3 goes the other way. Its gain over the first test is +0.006 as reported, but +0.016 to +0.028 at a shared mix.
3. The 0.959 figure rests on the 2-of-3 ticket_link rate from only 3 questions.

No verdict changes. The level rule passes at either mix (0.959 ≥ 0.925). Rules 1 and 2 keep wide margins (v9 − v4 = 0.375, v9 − v8 = 0.248). Rule 4 stays unmet (+0.041 at the first test's mix). v10 is 1.000 at both mixes.
verdict.corrected:
The write-up should state:

"The new set has 3 ticket_link questions; the first test had 7. Both sets were drawn with the same rule (fresh, at most 8 units per kind; ticket units are filled after the action and pr units), so this is a property of the draw, not a departure.

All of v9's ticket_link misses in either test are status questions in writer 1's wording ('where that other ticket currently stands'). In the writer-1 runs these went 0 of 6. The only drawn-set misses, one in each test, are status questions that drew writer 1's wording. Assignee questions and writer 2's status wording were always answered correctly. With fewer ticket_link questions, the new set gave fewer chances for this one failure.

At a shared mix of kinds, v9 does not do better on the new set:
- With the first test's mix: drawn v9 0.959 (v9n 0.944, v10 1.000, v4 0.584, v8 0.711).
- With the new set's mix, the first test scores 0.984, against 0.979 on the new set.
- So the new set is 0.005 to 0.016 below the first test, not 0.004 above. This is within noise.

For writer 1, all of the reported gain from 0.922 to 0.958 comes from the mix: 0.918 against 0.922 at the first test's mix, 0.958 against 0.957 at the new set's mix. For writer 3, the mix hides a small gain: 0.900 against 0.872 at the first test's mix, against a reported 0.878.

The mix-adjusted figures use the new set's 2-of-3 ticket_link rate, which rests on only 3 questions.

No verdict changes. At the first test's mix, v9 is 0.959, which still meets the 0.925 level rule. Rules 1 and 2 keep wide margins. Rule 4 is still not met (+0.041). v10 is 1.000 at both mixes."

findings.title: Rules 7 and 5 reuse the first run's training rows, so rule 7 is met 'again' by construction
findings.evidence: run_replication.sh runs `ask` only for mdrep, mdrepchanged and mdrep_w1 to w3. `plan` then reads the mdtrain and mdtrainv9 factbank_v*.jsonl rows written at 16:49 to 16:53 in the first test, unchanged since. The rule-7 numbers are therefore identical to the first test's (48 questions: v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993), and so is the training side of rule 5 (201 questions: v9 and v10 0.993). Code, lessons and form caches are unchanged (the training form caches use prompt bf3f84a670bd43be), so regenerating these rows would give the same values.
findings.impact: There is no bias, but the claim that rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 were met again overstates the new evidence. Only rules 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the test-set side of rule 5, are new observations; rule 7 repeats the first test's result.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every part of the finding checks out.

1. The pre-registered script (docs/benchmarks/factbank_plan/run_replication.sh, committed in 9c268e6, identical to plan9/run_rep.sh) runs `ask` only for mdrep, mdrepchanged and mdrep_w1 to w3. The frozen run_test.sh also re-asked mdtrain and mdtrainv9 (and mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm). `plan` is still given `--train $S/mdtrain --train-all $S/mdtrainv9`.
2. In those folders, factbank_v4/v8/v9/v9n/v10.jsonl were last written between 16:49:43 and 16:53:11 on 2026-10-09. That is during the first test (mdplan/plan_report.json is from 16:57). The replication ran from 19:15 to 19:27.
3. `plan_test` and `measure` in src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py only read those jsonl rows. Rule 7 uses the training data (`t`) alone. Rule 5 compares the new test set (`h`) with the 201 training questions (`ta`).
4. In mdrep/plan_report.json, the whole `training` and `training_all` dicts are identical to the ones in mdplan/plan_report.json and in the frozen docs/benchmarks/factbank_plan/plan_report.json:
   - 48 questions: v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993.
   - 201 questions: v4 0.822, v9 0.993, v10 0.993.
5. `git diff 7017046 -- src` is empty, and the lessons are frozen. Even if the rows had been regenerated, rule 7 measures the same frozen system on the same fixed training questions. So it cannot differ in a replication that changes only the documents. It is met again by construction.

The verdict still stands: rule 7 is genuinely met and the numbers are right. Only the claim that it was observed again overstates the evidence. The commit message of 7261461 says "Rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 met again", and neither summary.json mentions that the training rows were reused.

There is one more small gap. The pre-registration's prose says the script is the frozen one "with the seed, the output folder and the exclusion list changed, plus the single-writer runs". It does not say that the re-asking of the training and earlier sets was dropped. The script itself was committed before the run, so this is not a hidden change.
verdict.corrected: The write-up should say: "Rules 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the test-set side of rule 5, are new observations on the 50 new documents. They are all met: v9 0.979 and v10 1.000 on the test set, against 0.993 each on the 201 training questions (rule 5); changed copy 0.979 and 1.000, against 0.979 and 1.000 (rule 6). Rule 7 and the training side of rule 5 are not new evidence. The replication script did not re-answer the training questions. It reused the first test's rows in mdtrain and mdtrainv9, unchanged since 16:53 on 2026-10-09. With the code, lessons and training questions frozen, they could not differ in any case. So rule 7 (v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993 on the first 48 training questions) is met as before, by construction, not replicated. The replication criterion is still satisfied as pre-registered. Also, the run script differs from the frozen one in one more way than section 1 lists: it no longer re-asks the training and earlier sets."

findings.title: v4 (the baseline) did not give the same result, so the v9 minus v4 gap is smaller
findings.evidence: v4 (group mean): 0.510 then, 0.580 now (+0.070, beyond the pre-registration's 0.04 noise band). Per question: 0.42 then (21 of 50 fully right), 0.54 now (27). Averaged over every possible wording draw: 0.504 then, 0.619 now, so the rise comes from the questions themselves, not the draw. The main sources are person_count (4/8 then, 9/9 now) and action_owner_issues (0.375 then, 0.556 now). v9 − v4: +0.465 then, +0.399 now (per question +0.55 then, +0.44 now). Rule 3 right-for-the-right-reason, v4: 0.385 then, 0.471 now. v8 is stable (0.722 then, 0.720 now; per question 0.70 then, 0.72 now). v9 − v8: +0.253 then, +0.259 now.
findings.impact: 'The same results' holds for v8, v9 and v10, within noise, but not for v4. The write-up should give the planner's gain over v4 as roughly +0.40 to +0.47 across the two sets, not as a fixed +0.465. This supports the first review's point that v4's 0.510 came from those particular questions. Rules 1 to 3 still pass by 4 to 10 times their thresholds.

verdict.reason:
I recomputed every number with the repository's own scorer (factbank_multi.measure) over mdplan, mdrep and their _w1, _w2 and _w3 folders. All of them reproduce.

Group means:
- v4: 0.510 on the first test, 0.580 now (+0.070).
- v8: 0.722, then 0.720.
- v9: 0.975, then 0.979.
- Right for the right reason, v4: 0.385, then 0.471.

Per question:
- v4: 0.42 (21 of 50 fully right), then 0.54 (27 of 50).
- v8: 0.70, then 0.72.
- v9: 0.97, then 0.98.

Gaps:
- v9 − v4: +0.465, then +0.399 (per question +0.55, then +0.44).
- v9 − v8: +0.253, then +0.259.

The drawn wordings are all accounted for. Each drawn question's wording matches exactly one writer's run (mdplan 22 from writer 1 and 28 from writer 2; mdrep 29 and 21). Every drawn per-question score equals that writer's score, with 0 mismatches. So averaging the writer-1 and writer-2 runs gives the expected score over all possible draws.

On that average, v4 is 0.504 on the first test and 0.619 now. So the rise comes from the new questions, not the draw; the draw actually lowered v4 on the new set (0.580 against 0.619). The per-kind counts also match:
- person_count: 4 of 8, then 9 of 9.
- action_owner_issues: 3 of 8, then 5 of 9.

The rise is all in the combine group (0.391, then 0.615). The 0.619 average is close to the first review's prediction of 0.623 for v4 on this mix of kinds. That supports its point that v4's 0.510 came from those particular questions.

Two corrections to the finding:
1. "Rules 1 to 3 pass by 4 to 10 times their thresholds" is wrong. On the new set they pass by 3.99, 5.18 and 5.08 times (first test: 4.65, 5.06, 5.83). It should say "about 4 to 6 times".
2. +0.070 is beyond the pre-registration's 0.04 reading band. But that band describes one question flipping within a set, not drawing a different 50 questions. Between the two sets, 21 of 50 against 27 of 50 is not a significant difference (z = 1.2, p of about 0.23). So v4 differs by more than the stated band, but this is normal variation from sampling different questions, not v4 behaving differently.

The published documents (FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md and the README) give 0.510 and +0.465 as results of that one test set, which is still true. The finding only concerns the replication write-up, which has not been written yet (commit 7261461 holds raw results only).

- v10: 0.975, then 1.000. This one is +0.025, still inside the band.

findings.title: Of the 'six rules met again', rules 5, 6 and 7 add almost nothing new
findings.evidence: The training sections of docs/benchmarks/factbank_plan/plan_report.json and replication/plan_report.json are identical, every row (first 48 questions: v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993; all 201 training questions likewise). So rule 7 recomputes the same numbers. Rule 5's training side is the same too, which leaves only v9 and v10 on the test set >= 0.843, a weaker bar than the 0.925 level check. Rule 6: on mdrepchanged every v9, v9n and v10 score is identical to mdrep (13 changed expected answers, all 13 right), just as in the first test. Plans read names and dates rather than remember them, so the rule is close to guaranteed. Rules 1, 2 and 3 pass with margins of +0.399 (needs 0.10), +0.259 (needs 0.05) and +0.508.
findings.impact: The write-up should say which checks are new evidence: rules 1 to 3 and the level check on new documents, all far from their thresholds. It should say rules 5 to 7 are met by construction or by carrying over the first test's numbers, so 'six of six' does not overstate how much was tested.

verdict.reason:
I checked the data and the finding holds, apart from one claim that goes too far.

(1) The training data was not re-run. In docs/benchmarks/factbank_plan/plan_report.json and replication/plan_report.json, the `training` (48 questions) and `training_all` (201 questions) sections are byte-identical. That covers v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993, and the right-for-the-right-reason scores v4 0.743 and v9/v10 0.986. They are identical because run_replication.sh never re-answers training questions. Its final `plan` call reads $S/mdtrain and $S/mdtrainv9, whose factbank_v*.jsonl files were last written at 16:49–16:53. The new test set was not drawn until 19:15. So rule 7 does not recompute anything: it re-scores the first test's stored answers. The reviewer's word "recomputes" is slightly off, but that only makes the point stronger.

(2) Rule 5 compares the test set with the same old training score (0.993), so the bar is test ≥ 0.843. For v9 this is already implied by the level check (≥ 0.925). For v10 it adds only v10 ≥ 0.843, and v10 scored 1.000.

(3) Rule 6: on mdrepchanged, v9, v9n and v10 score exactly the same as on mdrep, question by question (0.979 / 0.958 / 1.000). 13 expected answers change, and each of those three arms gets all 13 right on the changed copy. The first test looked the same: 13 changed, 13 of 13 right, no differences. Where the finding goes too far is calling rule 6 "met by construction". It is a real measurement on new documents: v9's answer text differs on 14 of 50 questions between the two copies, so it had to produce the new values. The changed copy can also move a score: v4 lost person_first-002 (1→0) and dropped from 0.580 to 0.567. So rule 6 is an easy check for plans that read values from the documents, not an automatic pass.

(4) The margins are as stated. Rule 1: 0.979−0.580 = +0.399 (needs 0.10). Rule 2: 0.979−0.720 = +0.259 (needs 0.05). Rule 3: 0.979−0.471 = +0.508 (needs 0.10), and v9's right-for-the-right-reason score of 0.979 equals its plain score. Rule 7's margin, carried over, is 0.993 against 0.897.

The repository's write-up is still to come (FACTBANK_PLAN_REPLICATION.md contains only section 1). The commit message accurately says the rules are met by the pre-registered criteria, so nothing already published is wrong. The point is about how the coming write-up should describe the verdicts.
verdict.corrected: Add a line to the write-up's verdict, for example: "The six required rules are met again, but they are not six new tests. The replication did not re-answer the training questions. Rule 7 and the training side of rule 5 re-score the first test's stored training answers (48 questions: v4 0.927, v9 0.993, v10 0.993), so rule 7 is carried over unchanged. On the new documents, rule 5 only asks that v9 and v10 reach 0.843; the level check (v9 ≥ 0.925) already covers that for v9. Rule 6 is a weak check for the planner: its plans read names and dates from the documents. On the changed copy, v9, v9n and v10 give the same scores as on the test set, question by question, and get all 13 changed answers right, as in the first test. The changed copy can move a score: v4 lost one question, 0.580 → 0.567. The new evidence is rules 1–3 and the level check on 50 new documents. All of them clear their thresholds by wide margins: v9 − v4 = +0.399 (needs +0.10), v9 − v8 = +0.259 (needs +0.05), right for the right reason +0.508 (needs +0.10), and v9 0.979 against the 0.925 level."

findings.title: The glossary made a difference on the drawn set this time (v9n 0.958 against v9 0.979), unlike the first test
findings.evidence: In the first test v9 = v9n on every drawn question, and the write-up said the glossary 'was never exercised'. Here pr_issue-status-036 drew writer 1's 'What stage is the Linear ticket ... currently at?'; v9n answers it wrongly and v9 rightly. By wording, the glossary adds +0.021 (writer 1), 0 (writer 2) and +0.033 (writer 3) now, against +0.035, 0 and +0.029 then.
findings.impact: This is consistent with the first test's per-wording finding, but the write-up should not repeat 'v9 = v9n on the test'. The claim that no language model is needed holds only for writer 2's terse wording, in both tests.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every number and claim in the finding checks out against the data.

(1) Drawn set. In mdrep (and in mdrepchanged), v9 and v9n differ on exactly one question, pr_issue-status-036 (group: link). Its drawn wording is "What stage is the Linear ticket connected to pull request #18423 currently at?". In wordings.json that is the first entry of the pr_issue/status pair, so it is writer 1's wording. v9 follows linked_linear → status and answers "In Progress", which scores 1.0. v9n follows linked_linear → assignee and answers "Marco Diaz", which scores 0.0. One link question out of 16 is worth 1/16/3 = 0.021, which is the whole gap: v9 0.979 against v9n 0.958.

(2) First test. In mdplan, v9 and v9n have identical reasons and answers on all 50 questions. Both pr_issue-status questions there drew writer 2's wording ("what state's the Linear ticket tied to PR #... in rn?"). FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md line 229 says "the glossary was never exercised".

(3) It is the same wording both times. In the first test's writer-1 run, the only questions the glossary rescued were pr_issue-status-016 and -019, both in the "What stage..." wording; v9n read the assignee there too. So the replication's gap on the drawn set comes from the draw landing on a wording already known to need the glossary. It is not a new failure.

(4) By writer, from replication_summary.json:
- Replication: writer 1 0.958 − 0.937 = +0.021; writer 2 1.000 − 1.000 = 0; writer 3 0.878 − 0.845 = +0.033.
- First test: writer 1 0.922 − 0.887 = +0.035; writer 2 0.975 − 0.975 = 0; writer 3 0.872 − 0.843 = +0.029.

(5) Direction. On every question where v9 and v9n answer differently, v9n never scores better than v9. Each gap is within the pre-registered noise band (0.04 or less), but all of them point the same way. The pre-registered rules and the v9 ≥ 0.925 level do not involve v9n, so no verdict changes.

Nothing already published is wrong. The first test's write-up stands as a statement about that test, and it already limited "no language model is needed" to the terse writer (review point 4). The commit message of the raw-results commit 7261461 reports v9n 0.958 correctly, and the replication write-up has not been written yet. This finding is a correction for that coming write-up.

findings.title: Confirmation: v10 was never below v9, in either test or any wording
findings.evidence: Over 500 question-runs (mdplan, mdrep, their changed copies, and the three single-writer versions of each), v10 < v9 on 0 and v10 > v9 on 14. The lessons were unsure only on 4 writer templates: writer 1 ticket_link/status, pr_issue/due_date and pr_issue/status, and writer 3 pr_issue/due_date. The form changed the answer only on writer 1 ticket_link/status and writer 3 due-date.
findings.impact: The write-up can safely say that using the form only where the lessons are unsure did no harm on either set. It should add that the evidence for its benefit comes from 2 wordings.

verdict.reason:
I couldn't refute it. Every number in the finding checks out when I re-score the rows with the repo's own_score, read-only, over all 10 folders: mdplan, mdplanchanged, mdplan_w1/w2/w3, mdrep, mdrepchanged and mdrep_w1/w2/w3, 50 questions each.

What checks out:
- Of 500 question-runs, v10 < v9 on 0 and v10 > v9 on 14. On the right-for-the-right-reason measure it is also 0 below and 14 above.
- The lessons were unsure of the kind of answer (learned_kind None) on 31 runs. All of them fall on exactly the 4 templates named: writer 1 ticket_link/status (10), writer 1 pr_issue/due_date (9), writer 1 pr_issue/status (5) and writer 3 pr_issue/due_date (7).
- v10 chose a different plan from v9 on 17 runs, all on writer 1 ticket_link/status and writer 3 pr_issue/due_date:
  - 14 went from wrong to right;
  - 3 went from wrong to a different wrong answer: first-test ticket_link-status-039 (ENG-4823), which answered "ENG-4822" under v9 and "Done" under v10 when "In Review" was expected, in mdplan, mdplanchanged and mdplan_w1.
- On writer 1's pr_issue/due_date and pr_issue/status, v9 was already right, and v10 gave the same answers.

Three points the finding leaves out, which the write-up needs:

1. "Using the form only where the lessons are unsure" is not exactly how v10 works. In plans.answer, the form's kind is used only when the lessons are unsure. But its field filter applies whenever the form's kind matches the kind being used. That was 460 of the 500 runs, where the lessons were sure and the form agreed. On those 460 the filter never changed a plan. In 9 runs the form disagreed with sure lessons and was ignored.

2. The 14 runs are not 14 independent cases. The drawn and changed folders repeat wordings that are also in the single-writer folders: ticket_link-status-038 counts three times, in mdrep, mdrepchanged and mdrep_w1. The 14 runs reduce to 12 distinct question-and-wording cases plus one changed-information copy. They come from 2 wordings, across 7 tickets and 6 pull requests.

3. "No harm" does not hold beyond these two sets. On the earlier set mdfresh (the retest), v10 loses pr_issue-assignee-029: the lessons were unsure, the form said "key" with the field owner, and the answer went from "Jada Williams" (right) to "ENG-8421". FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md already reports this loss. The other earlier sets (mdtrain, mdtrainv9, mdtest, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm) show no loss, and gains of 4 on mdwords and 1 on mdblind.

Nothing published is wrong. The replication write-up has not been written yet (commit 7261461 holds raw results only, "write-up to follow"), and the first write-up already reports the mdfresh loss.
